title: steering-config-serialization-and-sanity-harness
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note records a compact, implementation-focused proposal for: (1) canonical serialization formats we accept for routing/steering configuration (YAML-first, JSON-compatible), (2) validation rules and a lightweight JSON Schema/semantics to enforce safety, and (3) a sanity/rollout harness (local + control-plane) that the platform-engineering team can use to progressively enable new steering rules across environments (staging -> prod-canary -> prod).

Why a separate document?
We have many related playbooks that talk about routing logic and progressive deployments. This file focuses narrowly on the serialization surface and the runtime safety checks needed to avoid mass traffic misroutes during rollout. The goal is to make configs: compact, human-editable, machine-validated, and robust to accidental operator mistakes.

High-level constraints (non-exhaustive):
- Single source format: authors will write YAML (anchors allowed) and the control plane canonicalizes to compact JSON for storage/compare.
- Backwards compatibility: fields may be marked required/deprecated; runtime will accept older opt-in variants for 12 months after deprecation notice.
- Deterministic semantics: order of conditions must be explicit when needed; undef behavior avoided.
- Safety-first: configs that can cause traffic loss (empty backends, unreachable region) must fail validation unless explicitly gated with "force: true" and an approval ticket.

Summary of the authoring model
- Authors create a steering YAML file describing one logical rule set (named object). Each rule set can contain multiple ordered steps; each step has match conditions, actions (route, mirror, enrich), and metadata about rollout.
- The control plane runs a two-phase validation: static schema checks + dynamic environment checks. Static rules are enforced locally (lint, json-schema); dynamic checks require querying inventories (region presence, model compatibility).

Example steering YAML (illustrative)
---
name: mobile-us-latency-steer
description: Route short-seq mobile traffic to low-latency variant in us-west, fallback to regular in other regions
version: 2025-02-11
steps:
  - id: primary-us-west
    priority: 10
    match:
      headers:
        user-agent: 
          - "MobileApp/*"
      path_prefix: "/v1/generate"
      max_tokens: 512
    action:
      type: route
      target: redwood-models/rt-lowlatency-v2
      region_preference: ["us-west-2"]
    rollout:
      mode: gradual
      schedule:
        - {percent: 5, duration_minutes: 60}
        - {percent: 25, duration_minutes: 30}
        - {percent: 100, duration_minutes: 10}
    safety_hard_gates:
      - backend_healthy: true
      - region_capacity: true
    telemetry_checks:
      - request_error_rate_threshold: 0.01
      - latency_p50_increase_threshold_ms: 50
  - id: mirror-experiments
    priority: 5
    match: {headers: {x-experiment: ["latency-probe"]}}
    action: {type: mirror, target: experiments/lowlatency-shadow}
    rollout: {mode: immediate}
---

Key fields explained (author view)
- name (string): unique within org. used in UI and audit logs.
- version (string/semver-ish): author increments with major semantic changes. Stored with semantic comparisons in the control plane.
- steps (ordered list): execution proceeds top-down; each step with higher priority runs before lower. Explicit priority numeric handles reorder without reindexing.
- match: a small domain-specific matcher supporting header patterns, path prefixes, query predicates, client-geolocation, and token-based attributes (e.g., customer_tier).
- action.type: route | mirror | enrich | deny | rewrite. route requires target; enrich may call a function/tool.
- rollout: {mode: immediate|gradual|manual}; schedule for gradual is an ordered list of percent buckets.
- safety_hard_gates: declarative checks that must be true for any rollout to proceed (backend health, capacity, feature-flag presence).
- telemetry_checks: runtime-derived constraints evaluated during canary windows (error rate, latency regressions, model-quality deltas).

Canonical JSON Schema (condensed, used for static lint)
Note: actual runtime allows a few convenience aliases. This snippet is the authoritative subset for CI/linting.
- top-level: object with required [name, steps]; optional [description, version, tags]
- steps: array(minItems=1) of objects with required [id, match, action, rollout] and optional [priority, safety_hard_gates, telemetry_checks]
- match.headers: map<string, array<string|pattern>>
- action: object with required [type], when type==route then required [target]
- rollout.mode: enum("immediate","gradual","manual"); if gradual then schedule present and each schedule item has percent (1-100) and duration_minutes (>0)

Validation & linting rules (checks in pre-commit + control plane static stage)
1) Unique rule name check across same service namespace.
2) Step ids must be unique within a rule.
3) Percent schedules must be increasing and final percent==100 for gradual unless finality_disabled: true present with documented approval.
4) All referenced targets must exist in the backend registry and have a compatible model contract (e.g., input schema, supported sequence length).
5) No conflicting side-effect actions in same step (e.g., route and deny together).
6) Anchors and aliases resolved: YAML is canonicalized before semantic comparison.
7) Size checks: max 50 steps or config rejected for being too complex — recommend splitting into multiple rule sets.

Dynamic (control-plane runtime) checks before any rollout begins
- Backend health: last probe within 30s and > 95% successful probes in 5m window.
- Region capacity: system forecast indicates available GPU capacity at target region for the scheduled rollout percent.
- Model compatibility: bincompat with current serving runtime (quantization settings, kv-cache format).
- Dependencies: if action.enrich references a tool/feature-flag, that must be enabled.

Safety/rollout harness behavior
- Local authoring: developer runs "rw-steer lint <file>" which enforces JSON Schema + quick registry checks via the auth-token.
- Preflight in CI: server-side preflight validates against a copy of live inventory and posts a preflight artifact with warnings (non-blocking) and failures (blocking). The CI artifact includes: failed checks, suggested fixes, and a dry-run of the canary schedule (estimated traffic numbers per region).
- Gradual rollout controller: the control plane orchestrates buckets. Each percent bucket is implemented by probabilistic routing in the edge layer (consistent hashing + override tables) or by sticky session sampling when applicable.
- Canary windows: for each bucket the system keeps a canary window (duration_minutes) and evaluates telemetry_checks. If any telemetry_check breaches its bound, the controller automatically pauses and rolls back to previous stable percent. An on-call alert is fired with a diagnostic bundle.

Automatic rollback policy (default)
- Failure triggers: request_error_rate increases by > double baseline and absolute delta > 0.02, or p50 latency regressions > telemetry_checks.threshold, or health probes fail.
- Rollback action: immediate revert to previous percent (or 0% if first bucket).
- Human override path: SRE/owner can promote with manual approval flow but must attach a mitigation plan for the next bucket. All overrides are logged and require a ticket with triage window <24h.

Operational runbooks (concise)
- Preflight failure (static): fix and re-lint; if false positive, open PLAT-1973 label and attach CI artifact.
- Runtime breach during canary: controller pauses, post diagnostic bundle to #platform-incidents, tag owner and the PR author. Escalate to SRE if rollback does not restore SLOs in 10 minutes.
- Emergency kill: if rule misroutes >1% of total production traffic unexpectedly, we have an automated kill-switch that sets rule to passive and reverts to traffic-safety-fallback policy.

Examples of common error messages (improve UX)
- "schedule.invalid: percent values must be strictly increasing and final value must be 100 (or finality_disabled=true)"
- "target-not-found: experiments/lowlatency-shadow not found in backend registry"
- "region-capacity: us-west-2 insufficient capacity for requested percent=25 (need 3x current)"

Testing suggestions for authors
- Unit tests: assert serialization roundtrip (YAML -> JSON -> YAML) and equality; assert canonical ordering of step priorities.
- Integration: run with a staging inventory using realistic capacity numbers. Use the shadow mode (rollout.mode: immediate + action: mirror) to capture changes without risk.
- Chaos test: run the canary window with artificially injected 503s to ensure auto-rollback path triggers and alerting works.

Open questions / future work
- Should we support declarative weight-splitting across multiple backends inside a single step (e.g., 80% backendA, 20% backendB)? Proposal: yes, but wire-level and telemetry must be per-backend to make rollback granular.
- Long-lived gradual rollouts with seasonal capacity shifts: consider capacity-reservation primitives on the scheduling API.
- Rollout auditability: provide a UI timeline with percent, metrics, and user approvals embedded.

Appendix: small CLI examples
- lint: rw-steer lint mobile-us-latency-steer.yaml
- preflight upload: rw-steer preflight --env staging mobile-us-latency-steer.yaml -> returns preflight-id
- promote: rw-steer promote --id preflight-id --to prod-canary
- abort: rw-steer abort --rule mobile-us-latency-steer

Notes for reviewers
- This is a draft intended to be implementable by platform-engineering + serving-runtime teams. Please call out missing edge cases (authz, multi-tenant namespace collisions) and practical UX improvements (clearer error text, better default schedule).

Authors: Maya Chen (platform-engineering)
Reviewed-by: Rafael Ortiz, Priya Nambiar
